comment: Break-glass access needs minimum emergency-access governance. The LHR appropriately requires emergency/break-glass access and full audit capture, but audit logging alone does not define when an override is justified, what scope of data may be accessed, how long the override lasts, or how inappropriate use is subsequently detected and reviewed.

citation.raw: §Appendix C - Lifelong Health Record, p. 161, Requirement 13.

public.text: Break-glass access needs minimum emergency-access governance. The LHR appropriately requires emergency/break-glass access and full audit capture, but audit logging alone does not define when an override is justified, what scope of data may be accessed, how long the override lasts, or how inappropriate use is subsequently detected and reviewed.
public.suggestedRevision: Define a technology-neutral minimum break-glass profile requiring authenticated actor identity, documented reason/purpose, proportionate and time-bounded access, complete audit provenance, and post-hoc review or monitoring for inappropriate use. Where appropriate and lawful, support transparency or notification to the individual. National law and clinical policy should determine qualifying emergency circumstances and category-specific restrictions.
